data.narrative:
Anatar, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Kaia Rhodes, is evaluated against a peer universe comprising one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private robotics firms at similar or adjacent stages. The peer set includes established names such as Exotec, Nimble Robotics, Agile Robots, and Divergent, providing market-informed context for frontier-stage capital deployment in autonomous systems.

The peer-median method, applied across seven same-sector comparables spanning Series B through Series D, yields an implied valuation of $1.6B. The peer range spans $1.0B to $2.0B, with representative transactions including Exotec and Generalist AI at $2.0B (Series D and B respectively), Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B (Series B), and both Dexterity and Hadrian at $1.6B (Series B and D). This single triangulation method, the only applicable approach given available data, carries material weight in the absence of discernible revenue multiples, comparable M&A precedent, or disclosed financial metrics for Anatar.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $1.9B, centered on $1.6B. Key uncertainties include Anatar's specific revenue run rate, customer concentration, technology differentiation relative to peers, and capital efficiency post-Series C. The single-method derivation limits confidence; incorporation of revenue multiples or DCF analysis would require disclosure of financial performance currently unavailable. Stage-adjusted discount to the $2.0B outliers appears warranted pending Series D progression.
